_note: party-kinds-accepted-per-case-type. One vocabulary of party kinds for the fleet, held here, and a declaration per record type of which kinds it accepts. pipelinq holds no case type and no editor for one: the acceptance target is an opaque `<app>:<schema>:<type>` string it stores and matches and never interprets.

partyKind.title: Party kind
partyKind.description: One kind of party: aanvrager, gemachtigde, belanghebbende, melder. A consuming app declares none of its own and ships no list of them.

code.title: Code
code.description: The stable code a link and an acceptance point at.

label.title: Label
label.description: What a handler reads in the picker and on the record.

description.title: Description
description.description: What this kind means, so two municipalities do not quietly mean different things by one word.

identityShapes.title: Identity shapes
identityShapes.description: The shapes a party of this kind may take. `none` says a party of this kind needs no account of any kind: making such a party notifiable belongs to the notification dialect openregister owns, and deliberately does not live here.

fieldSet.title: Field set
fieldSet.description: The party field set this kind carries, by its partyKind code.

maxPerRecord.title: Maximum per record
maxPerRecord.description: 1 for a kind one record holds once, such as an aanvrager. Absent or 0 means unbounded, such as a belanghebbende. A second holder of a single kind is refused on the write, naming the party that already holds it.

active.title: Active
active.description: Whether the kind is offered in the picker. An inactive kind keeps resolving on links already written, so a retired kind does not take the meaning of old links with it.

partyKindAcceptance.title: Party kind acceptance
partyKindAcceptance.description: Which party kinds one record type of one consuming app accepts, in the order the consuming app declared them. The declaration is the consuming app's policy; the object is pipelinq's.

recordType.title: Record type
recordType.description: The record type this acceptance is for, named `<app>:<schema>:<type>`. Stored and matched as an opaque string: pipelinq does not parse it, does not validate the app id and does not learn what a case type is.

kinds.title: Kinds
kinds.description: The accepted kinds, in the declared order. The first is what most handlers will take, so the order is part of the declaration and is not re-sorted for display.

partyLink.title: Party link
partyLink.description: One party on one record under one kind. Where an acceptance exists for the record's type, a kind it does not name is refused on every write path alike: the picker, an import, an API call and a flow. Where no acceptance is declared, nothing is refused, so an app that has declared nothing keeps working.

kind.title: Kind
kind.description: The party kind code this party holds on this record.

recordType.title: Record type
recordType.description: The type of the record the party is linked to, as `<app>:<schema>:<type>`. Opaque to pipelinq.

recordId.title: Record
recordId.description: The record the party is linked to.

validFrom.title: Valid from
validFrom.description: When the party started holding this kind on this record.

validUntil.title: Valid until
validUntil.description: When they stopped. Replacing a single-kind holder is an explicit act: end the existing link, then write the new one.
